title: PMT stays open: the expm1 |tau|<1 op-graph wall and its ceilings
status_plain: PMT's catalogue row is open and the source says so twice in the same line: "Row STAYS OPEN". The residual is localised to Excel's expm1 on the |tau|<1 branch, characterised as a bespoke, toward-zero-biased inline expm1 whose op-graph matches no tested family and no open-source implementation. Every figure in this record is a ceiling over a searched family of candidate models on an instrument corpus, not a PMT-versus-Excel pass rate, and reading any of them as a pass rate mis-scopes it badly: 0/1350 in particular is a GOOD result, meaning zero non-correctly-rounded rows, and reads as catastrophic if mistaken for a pass count. Three claims were retracted here, including a whole substrate verdict, and the retractions are part of the record.

counts.ambiguity_note: READ THE SIGN OF THIS FIGURE CAREFULLY. `0/1350` counts rows where Excel's log1p was NOT correctly rounded. Zero such rows were found, which is the source's evidence that Excel's PMT log1p IS correctly rounded. Rendered as a pass rate of 0 per cent it inverts its meaning completely. `passed: 0` here means zero non-correctly-rounded rows, not zero passing rows.

open_question: Whether the |tau|<1 expm1 op-graph is closable at all. The source's verdict is that it is a genuine faithful-rounding boundary with a ceiling of 165 of 234 and is "NOT black-box-closable".
reader_warning: None of the counts in this record is a PMT-versus-Excel pass rate. They are ceilings over searched families and instrument checks on a 234-row corpus the pins were solved from. `0/1350` counts non-correctly-rounded rows and finding zero of them is the good outcome. `3840/3840` and `234/234` score instruments, not PMT. `2285/4040` scores a research model and the source forbids reporting it as an OxFunc pass rate.
